newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SHARES MIXED, NO BIG GAINS IN SIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SHARES MIXED, NO BIG GAINS IN SIGHT.

text.p: Lithuania shares were mixed on Friday and dealers said that no big gains were looming on the horizon.
"We expect more of the same next week...up and down and no really big price increases," Tomas Andrejauskas of brokerage house Suprema told Reuters.
Dealers say that the market is in a state of flux in the wake of shareholders' meetings as some investors bail with dividends in hand while others snap at cheap shares.
But brokers said that one positive sign was an increase in the activity of banking shares.
"When the banks pick up, the rest of the market usually folows," one dealer said.
Dealers said that unexpectedly good 1996 results from the sector, which was rocked by a crisis late in 1995, have helped to restore confidence in banking shares.
Banks accounted for the lion's share of central market activity, turning over 1.26 million litas.
Overall central market volume was over 1.7 million litas and the Litin A index dipped 11.16 points to 2,568.99.
Hermis Bank was by far the most active listing in trade of almost 1.1 million litas at the unchanged price of 190.00 litas.
Several blue chips eased, including Birzai Dairy, which fell to 9.00 litas from 9.50 litas in trade of only 684.00 litas.
The session's few gainers included Ragutis brewery, which climbed to 18.40 litas from 17.60 litas in trade of 19,500 litas.
Block trades reached over 1.7 million litas.
